entries.title: Psalms 73:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A clean heart - To all true Israelites, who love God, and serve him in spirit and truth.

entries.title: Psalms 73:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My feet - My faith in God's providence, was almost overthrown.

entries.title: Psalms 73:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No bands - They are not dragged to death, by the sentence of the magistrate, which they deserve.

entries.title: Psalms 73:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: As other men - As good men frequently are.

entries.title: Psalms 73:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Against - Against God, blaspheming his name, and deriding his providence. Walketh - Using all manner of liberty, reproaching all sorts of persons.

entries.title: Psalms 73:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Turn - To this wicked company. Waters - And partake of the same prosperity with their leaders. God seems to give them a full cup of consolation, as if he would wring out all his blessings upon them.

entries.title: Psalms 73:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Behold - These seem to be the words of the psalmist, summing up the matter.

entries.title: Psalms 73:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In vain - Hence I was sometimes tempted, to think that religion was a vain, unprofitable thing. True religion is here described by its two principal parts, the cleansing of the heart, and the hands.

entries.title: Psalms 73:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Offend - By grieving, discouraging and tempting them to revolt from God.

entries.title: Psalms 73:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To know - To find out the reason of this providence.

entries.title: Psalms 73:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Until - 'Till I consulted the word of God. He alludes to the practice of those times, which was, in difficult cases to resort to God's sanctuary, and the oracle therein. Their end - There I learned that their prosperity was short.

entries.title: Psalms 73:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Terrors - With God's dreadful judgements unexpectedly seizing upon them.

entries.title: Psalms 73:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: They awake - Out of the pleasant dream of this vain life. Despise - Thou shalt make them despicable both to themselves and to all others; raise them to shame, and everlasting contempt. Image - All their felicity and glory, which shall be evidently discerned to be, no real or substantial thing, but a mere image or shadow.

entries.title: Psalms 73:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pricked - I was deeply wounded with disquieting thoughts.

entries.title: Psalms 73:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Nevertheless - Although I gave thee just cause to cast me off, yet thou didst continue thy care and kindness to me. Hast held - That my faith might not fail.

entries.title: Psalms 73:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Go a whoring - Those who revolt from thee, to work wickedness; which is called whoredom in scripture.
